newsitem.title: USA: Militia meet to plot U.S. government collapse.
newsitem.headline: Militia meet to plot U.S. government collapse.

text.p: Members of U.S. militia groups gathered on Thursday for the final day of a three-day convention during which they mapped out a strategy for the downfall of the government.

The convention, which began on Tuesday, was held at a hotel in Kansas City and included more than 20 delegates from as far away as New Jersey, North Dakota and Texas. Several delegates said they learned about the event over the Internet.
Some delegates to the "Third Continental Congress" said it had veered from its original goal to set up a provisional government for the day when the U.S. government collapses.

"We are now realising that the people are not educated enough. If we were to form an outline for a provisional government the people might be scared, they might demonise us, and we have come to realise that we do not have enough backing," said Scott Allen Woodring, a delegate from Fremont, Michigan.
Woodring said the convention had decided to form several committees to discuss ways in which to educate people.

"I think everybody can see with their own eyes ... that something's wrong in this country," Erich Morrow, a delegate from Ludwig, Arkansas, said. "We have to sit down, regroup, rethink and then come up with solutions to re-establish a republican form of government."

Ray Southwell, founder of the Northern Michigan Regional Militia and organiser of the convention, would not respond to repeated efforts to contact him. But he told the Kansas City Star newspaper that by uniting independent groups would be able to speak with a more powerful voice.
"If we do not come together, we will have anarchy," Southwell was quoted as saying.

Militia groups have sprouted up across the United States, mainly in rural areas. They shot to international prominence last year after the bombing of a federal building in Oklahoma City in which 168 people died.
